$comment: The evidence specification (Gate 5 Phase 2, APR-JE-030). One source for the procedures (docs/device-testing/*.md are generated from it), the scaffolded evidence records and the release gate's validation. Changing an item here changes the checklists, the templates and what the gate demands.

E1.name: Browser emulation
E1.meaning: Automated and emulated: Playwright engines, device descriptors, viewport and forced-colours emulation, a CI run
E1.mayClaim: behaves as expected in this engine under emulation
E1.neverClaim: anything about a physical device, a screen reader or a person's experience

E2.name: Human testing on a desktop browser
E2.meaning: A person, on a real desktop or laptop, in a real desktop browser (Safari on a Mac, Firefox, Chrome), including desktop screen readers
E2.mayClaim: verified by hand in this browser on this computer
E2.neverClaim: how a phone or tablet behaves

E3.name: Human testing on a physical device
E3.meaning: A person holding a real phone or tablet (model, operating-system version and browser version recorded)
E3.neverClaim: anything about other devices or versions

attestation: I performed this test myself in the environment described in this record and the outcomes are my own observations.

needs.label: a successful CI run for the release commit

page-basics.title: Every page: it loads and reads properly

items.text: Open the page from the start of the session (address bar or a link). Wait for it to finish loading.
items.expect: Text, photographs and the two typefaces appear; no error message, no blank area where an image should be.

items.text: Look at the whole page by scrolling from top to bottom, in the orientation(s) named for this target.
items.expect: No sideways scrolling, nothing cut off, nothing drawn over other text or controls.

items.text: Read the headings and body text at the device's normal settings, without zooming.
items.expect: Text is comfortably legible (size and contrast) and keeps its normal line breaks.

items.text: Use the header links (and the brand link and footer links) to move to other pages, then use the browser's Back and Forward.
items.expect: Each link opens the right page; Back and Forward return to the page you left.

items.text: Look at every photograph on the page.
items.expect: Each photograph is shown, sharp enough, not stretched or squashed.

items.text: Narrow screens: tap or press the menu button, then close the menu. Wide screens: confirm the header links are visible.
items.expect: The menu opens and closes; the button's state is clear; the links are all reachable when it is open.

items.text: On each page look at the header link for the page you are on.
items.expect: The current page is marked as current.

items.text: Press Tab once at the top of a page (keyboard or switch access if available), then Enter on the skip link that appears.
items.expect: A skip link appears first, becomes visible, and moves you past the header to the main content.

home-hero.title: Home page hero: poster, clip, Pause (once per session)

items.text: Open the Home page and watch the hero for 20 seconds. Record in the note whether you saw the still poster, the looping clip, or a poster that slowly pushes in, and the window width in CSS pixels if you know it.
items.expect: What is shown matches the design for this width: phones and narrow windows get the poster; widths of 960 px and more get the clip where the browser can play it.

items.text: If a Pause button is shown, press it and press it again.
items.expect: Pause stops the motion and Resume restarts it; the button's label changes and it is easy to hit.

items.text: Turn on the system setting 'Reduce Motion' (or 'Remove animations'), reload the Home page, and watch the hero.
items.expect: Nothing loops or pushes in; the still poster is shown.

items.text: If the clip does not play in this browser, look at what the hero shows instead.
items.expect: A poster is shown and nothing looks broken (no empty black box, no play icon).

items.text: On the Menu page use the category strip (Small plates ... Sweet & tea): scroll it sideways if it overflows, then choose a category.
items.expect: The strip scrolls; each link jumps to its section and the heading is not hidden under the header.

items.text: On the Menu page read a few dish names, descriptions and prices.
items.expect: Names, descriptions and prices are legible and line up; the heat markers are understandable.

items.text: On the Our story page read the opening and one later section.
items.expect: Text and pictures sit in a sensible order; nothing overlaps.

items.text: On the Visit page read the address and the opening-hours table.
items.expect: The address and every day's hours are readable and the day labels do not touch the times, also when you enlarge the text.

items.text: On the Visit page press the telephone number.
items.expect: The device offers to call the number shown (+1 555 0100 188 is a sample number: cancel the call).

items.text: On the Order online page read 'How ordering works', Pickup and Allergies.
items.expect: The steps and notices are readable in order; the page says clearly that ordering is a sample.

items.text: On the Home page scroll through 'Order these first', the kitchen story, the visit strip and the order band.
items.expect: Every section is readable and every link in them works.

mobile-device.title: Phone and tablet handling (once per session)

items.text: Tap the menu button, the header links, the telephone number and a menu category link with a finger.
items.expect: Each is easy to hit on the first try; no neighbouring control is triggered by mistake.

items.text: Rotate the device to landscape and back on the Home, Menu and Visit pages.
items.expect: The layout adapts without clipping or sideways scrolling; nothing stays in the old orientation.

items.text: Increase the system text size (Dynamic Type on iOS, Font size on Android) to a large setting and reopen the Home and Visit pages.
items.expect: Text grows without overlapping or being cut off; the menu button still works.

items.text: Turn on Low Power Mode / Battery Saver, and Low Data Mode / Data Saver, reload the Home page.
items.expect: The page still works; the hero shows the poster if the browser blocks the clip.

items.text: Scroll down and up so the browser's address bar hides and shows again.
items.expect: The header and the hero do not jump or leave a gap.

tablet-wide.title: Tablet and wide-window behaviour (once per session)

items.text: At a width of 960 CSS pixels or more (tablet landscape or a wide window) open the Home page.
items.expect: The hero uses the clip path (the loop plays) or the poster fallback; either is shown cleanly.

items.text: If this browser cannot play the WebM clip (Safari), watch whether the MP4 version plays.
items.expect: The MP4 plays, or the poster is shown; nothing looks broken. Record which in the note.

items.text: On an iPad try Split View or Slide Over (or narrow the window) and rotate.
items.expect: The layout reflows at each width without sideways scrolling.

items.text: Using only the keyboard, press Tab repeatedly from the top of the page to the end of the page.
items.expect: Every link and button is reached once, in the order you read them; nothing is skipped.

items.text: While tabbing, look at where the focus is.
items.expect: The focused element always has a clearly visible outline or highlight; it is never hidden under the header.

items.text: Tab forward through the page and Shift+Tab backward again.
items.expect: Focus never gets stuck; Shift+Tab walks the same order backwards.

keyboard-session.title: Keyboard-only: menu, Pause, skip link (once per session)

items.text: On a narrow window use Enter or Space on the menu button, Tab through the links, then press Escape.
items.expect: The menu opens, its links can be tabbed in order, Escape closes it and focus returns to the menu button.

items.text: On the Home page Tab to the Pause button and press Enter or Space.
items.expect: Pause works from the keyboard and shows its state.

items.text: Press Tab first on each page and activate the skip link with Enter.
items.expect: Focus moves into the main content.

zoom-responsive.title: Responsive layouts, zoom and text spacing

items.text: Zoom the page to 200 percent (browser zoom, or Settings > Display zoom).
items.expect: The page reflows into one column where needed; nothing is cut off; no sideways scrolling.

items.text: Zoom to 400 percent on a desktop browser (about 320 CSS pixels wide).
items.expect: Content stays readable in one column; only tables and code may scroll sideways (this site has none); nothing is clipped.

items.text: Enlarge only the text (Firefox: View > Zoom > Zoom Text Only; or the system text size) to the largest sensible size.
items.expect: Text grows and wraps; nothing overlaps; buttons keep their labels.

items.text: On a touch device pinch to zoom in on the Home and Menu pages.
items.expect: Pinch zoom works (the page does not block it) and the page stays usable.

items.text: Make the window or screen as narrow as you can (about 320 CSS pixels).
items.expect: The page still works in one column, with the menu button visible.

items.text: If you have a text-spacing tool or bookmarklet (line height 1.5, letter spacing 0.12 em, word spacing 0.16 em), apply it on the Visit page and read the opening hours.
items.expect: The day labels and the times do not touch or overlap; nothing is cut off.

items.text: Turn on Reduce Motion in the operating system (or the browser) and open the Home page.
items.expect: The hero shows the still poster; no continuous motion anywhere on the site.

items.text: With the connection slow or switched to a poor network (if you can), reload a page and watch the images load.
items.expect: Photographs appear without the layout jumping; text is readable while they load.

items.text: If the hero clip is blocked or does not play (Low Power Mode, an old browser), look at the hero.
items.expect: A poster is shown; the hero never stays empty.

items.text: Open the landmarks list (the screen reader's rotor, elements list or landmark gesture).
items.expect: Banner/header, navigation, main and footer (contentinfo) are listed and correctly named.

items.text: Open the headings list and step through the headings in order.
items.expect: There is one main heading and the other headings follow a sensible order that matches the page.

items.text: Step through every link and button.
items.expect: Each one is announced with a clear name and its role (link or button); the current page link says it is current; no 'link' or 'button' without a name.

items.text: Step through the photographs.
items.expect: Meaningful photographs have a short description; purely decorative ones are skipped.

items.text: Read the page from top to bottom with the screen reader's read-all command.
items.expect: The text is read in the same order you see it; no hidden or duplicate text is read.

screen-reader-session.title: Screen reader: controls and key content (once per session)

items.text: Move to the first item on a page.
items.expect: The skip link is announced first and moves you to the main content.

items.text: On a narrow window or phone, find the menu button and open and close it.
items.expect: The button announces its state (expanded or collapsed) and the links appear in the reading order when open.

items.text: On the Home page find the Pause button.
items.expect: It is announced with its name and state (pressed or not) and works.

items.text: On the Visit page read the address, the opening-hours table and the telephone link.
items.expect: The address is read in order, the hours table is read row by row with day and time, the telephone link says it is a link to call (a sample number).

items.text: On the Order online page read 'How ordering works' and the notices.
items.expect: The steps are read in order; the page says clearly that ordering is a sample.

items.text: While using the site, notice any unexpected announcements, repeated text or silence.
items.expect: None; or every surprise is written up as a finding.
